entities.summary:
Anton von Prokesch-Osten was an Austrian diplomat, statesman and general who played a crucial role in the unification of Austria-Hungary in the late 19th century. Born into a wealthy and influential family, von Prokesch-Osten was educated at the Theresianum in Vienna and later served in the Austro-Hungarian Army, rising to the rank of general. He was a key figure in the negotiations that led to the Ausgleich, a compromise between the Austrian and Hungarian delegations that preserved the unity of the empire but granted greater autonomy to Hungary.

Von Prokesch-Osten's diplomatic career was marked by a series of high-profile postings, including service as ambassador to Italy and Bulgaria. He was a strong advocate for the unification of South Slavs and played a key role in the negotiations that led to the formation of the South Slavic Committee, a precursor to the modern-day Visegrád Group.

Despite his many accomplishments, von Prokesch-Osten's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of his contemporaries. However, his contributions to the unification of Austria-Hungary and the promotion of South Slavic unity remain significant, and his diplomatic skills and strategic thinking continue to be studied by historians and scholars today.

In 1876, von Prokesch-Osten died in Vienna, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most important diplomats of his era. His commitment to the principles of unity, cooperation, and diplomacy continues to inspire scholars and policymakers alike.

The von Prokesch-Osten Foundation, established in his memory, continues to promote the values of cooperation and diplomacy, providing scholarships and fellowships to students and researchers from around the world.
